Material-cache hits bypass the existing shallow-checkout safeguard used to determine whether validation evidence can bind. Other inspected boundaries retain raw-history Git reads, live ref resolution and reader-owned snapshot copies.

Compared the implementation with smaller single-cache alternatives documented in D1. Measurements justify addressing all four repeated-work sites. Process-local maps avoid a new persistence or authority layer, and broader graph recomputation remains excluded. The choice depends on cacheable results being immutable and misses being coordinated; F1-F4 require corrections within this same small design.

findings.action: The material-cache key omits repository shallowness and caches unreadable results. materialSetDigestAt first checks repositoryIsShallow and also returns MaterialDigestUnreadable on Git failures, so its result is not solely a function of root, commit and inputs. After a shallow checkout is unshallowed without moving HEAD, the cached unreadable marker persists; conversely, a cached successful digest bypasses the shallow-checkout rejection if the repository becomes shallow at the same HEAD. Transient read failures also persist until eviction or process restart. Recheck repository eligibility before cache reuse, avoid retaining failed reads, and cover fixed-HEAD shallow-state transitions and recovery.

The snapshot cache retains incomplete snapshots after failing Git reads, contrary to R2. readReleaseSnapshotAtCommitUncached converts policy, fragment, directory-listing, notes and version-source read failures into snapshot gaps and ultimately returns nil error at line 784. Therefore this err == nil condition caches those failures indefinitely. For example, a transient fragment cat-file failure at lines 717-724 remains a gap after Git recovers. The new failure test removes the repository before the manifest read and does not cover these later failures. Track whether every required read completed and retry snapshots containing operational read failures while retaining genuinely content-derived invalidity.

Every failed commit peel is cached permanently as proof that the object is not a commit. A successful cat-file -t followed by a failed rev-parse does not establish that conclusion: an annotated tag can temporarily have an unavailable target object, or the peel command can fail operationally. Once the target is fetched or the failure repaired, resolving the unchanged tag still returns ErrReleaseTagNotCommit from the cached empty entry without retrying. Cache a negative result only when object inspection proves a non-commit target; leave failed or incomplete peels retryable and add recovery coverage.

Concurrent cache misses duplicate the work that R1, R2 and R4 require to occur once per process. The Load/compute/Store sequence has no per-key coordination: two graph workers can both miss line 293 and both invoke currentMaterialAt. The snapshot cache at release_manifest_integrity.go:643-653, tag-object cache at :381-401 and header cache at review_operation_view.go:37-58 use the same pattern. sync.Map protects the map but does not deduplicate computation. Coordinate in-flight work per key while preserving retry behavior for failures, and add barrier-controlled concurrent-miss tests; the added tests currently exercise sequential reuse only.
